previousItemsStillOpen: Photo r4 MAJOR 'stopped clock and contradicting readings': the six named faults are gone in the pictures. The clock runs (T+ 00:01:10 up to 8d 02:52:00, UT = launch + MET, the pad at 0), the ascent pulls 1.44 g at 86 % throttle, the entry pulls 0.68 g at 2.7 kPa with -168.6 m/s, the chutes view reads 1.00 g, lunar orbit has no impact miss, GEAR is DOWN when landed (HUD and SYS page), the failure reads 'burned through at 68.0 km' with the shield at 0 %, and no lab words are on screen. The same class of fault still shows in other readouts: mains pending at an 8 m/s sink, circular translunar and entry orbits, 30 m radar altitude when landed, and a constant 50 t mass. Finding 1 carries these at major.

Photo r4 minor 'HUD has no look of its own' (partly fixed): the left column and the altimeter now use the MFD's black glass, with tab titles and status edges. The bottom cluster is still five separate pieces in two materials with no shared housing: speed box, pitch/heading/roll strip, ball, SAS plate and gauge plate. It also stands 34 % of the frame tall in the middle of the screen. See finding 3.

Artifact r4 minor 'G-dose line pushes the tubes up' (partly fixed): the reentry vs entry-highg jump is gone, and the spec asserts it. But the line still appears and disappears with the flight state. The gauge panel's top edge is at y 598 on the pad and y 575 in the ascent (720p), so the throttle and g tubes jump 23 px at liftoff. The same jump happens between lowOrbit and reentry. See finding 4.

Artifact r4 minor 'Evidence: lab placeholder backdrop' (partly fixed): four HUD-over-real-renderer composites were added (real-ascent, real-lowOrbit, real-lunarSurface, real-reentry), the limb's ruled line is gone and the cabin clock matches its still. About 40 of the 56 pictures still sit over the grid-lattice sea, grey cylinders and flat faceted Moon. The integration's pad and splashdown stills (budget-pad-lift-off.png, budget-splashdown.png) are unused, and real-ascent pairs a HUD reading 9 220 m with a still from the 10-40 km ascent run. See finding 8.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\flight-ui\chutes-720p.png, chutes-4k.png, retrograde-hold-720p.png, retrograde-hold-4k.png; translunar-720p.png, translunar-4k.png; mfd-pages-native-reentry.png (ORB and SYS pages); mfd-pages-hover-720p.png, mfd-pages-hover-4k.png (FLT and LND pages); mfd-pages-4k.png (SYS); entry-highg-720p.png against reentry-720p.png
findings.defect: The headline contradictions are fixed, but a second look still finds readouts that cannot all be true, in five views. (1) Under chutes the capsule sinks at a steady 8.0 m/s at 1.00 g, which is a main-chute descent. Yet the top-right tile offers '10 Mains, cut chute · deploy chute, Space' as the next stage, so the mains are not out; on drogues alone the sink rate would be several times higher. (2) Translunar coast at T+ 1d 02:21: the ORBIT panel reads APOAPSIS 180.0 Mm and PERIAPSIS 180.0 Mm, period 9d 06:25 and vertical speed 0.0 m/s. That is a circular orbit at half the Moon's distance, but a coast a day after TLI is a long ellipse (Pe a few hundred km, Ap near 400 Mm) climbing at about 1.4 km/s. (3) In entry the MFD ORB page shows Ap 68.0 km, Pe 68.0 km, eccentricity 0.0000, period 1:25:42 and TIME TO AP T- 42:51. The HUD and the LND page beside it show -168.6 m/s and an impact 1 425 km ahead. (4) Landed on the Moon with the gear DOWN, the LND page reads RADAR ALT 30.0 m and the FLT tape 30.0 m. (5) The SYS page reads MASS 50.0 t in lunar orbit, on the surface after 59 % of the descent propellant has burned, and in entry where only the Kestrel capsule is left (ΔV total 0.0 m/s). (6) entry-highg is 20 km lower than the plain entry and pulls 11.2 g, but keeps its MET (T+ 8d 02:41:00), Mach 24.77, sink -168.6 m/s and 7 428.9 m/s.
findings.realReference: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\reentry-chutes\artemis2-mains.jpg is the phase the chutes numbers describe: a steady single-digit sink rate happens only on the mains (Orion and Apollo descend at about 8-9 m/s on mains and about 50-60 m/s on drogues). Mission trajectory displays and KSP's orbit panel always show the osculating orbit of the actual trajectory. During entry the periapsis lies below the surface, a translunar coast has e ≈ 0.97, and a landed LM's radar altitude reads about zero. The brief judges interface packages on 'correct information'.
findings.likelyCause: labs/flight-ui/main.ts SETUP (lines 172-181): `chutes` has `fired: 9`, so stage 10 (Mains) is still pending while `chutes: true` sets 1 g (line 357). The lab decorates readouts but not the osculating elements (apoapsisAltitude, periapsisAltitude, eccentricity, period, timeToApoapsis), so the FakeSim's circular conics show through (the hand-off states this as 'not fixed'). altitudeRadar is decorated only on the entry path (line 351). The vessel mass is the FakeSim's constant. entry-highg reuses the reentry scene and overrides only g, q and height.
findings.fixDirection: Fix it in the lab's decoration layer, as the clock was fixed. Chutes: `fired: 10` (mains ACTIVE, no next stage), or keep the drogues and set the sink to about 60 m/s at about 1 g. Translunar: Pe about 0.19 Mm, Ap about 400 Mm, e about 0.97, vertical about +1.4 km/s, horizontal about 0.4 km/s. Entry: the elements that 7 868 m/s at -1.2 degrees gives at 68 km, which are Pe about -70 km (below the surface, no time to Pe), Ap about 205 km and e about 0.02. Landed: altitudeRadar = the reference point's height above the pads (about 2-4 m). Mass: sum the remaining stage groups. entry-highg: MET about +90 s and Mach from the local speed of sound. Add spec checks for each case: landed means radar altitude under 10 m; any scene sinking faster than 50 m/s has its periapsis below its altitude; in the chutes scene the mains have fired; SYS mass falls between pad, orbit and entry.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\flight-ui\translunar-720p.png, translunar-4k.png (altimeter row against ORBIT SPEED); lowOrbit-720p.png, lowOrbit-4k.png, real-lowOrbit-720p.png, prograde-hold.png, map-lowOrbit-720p.png
findings.defect: The altimeter's second row shows the vertical and horizontal speed in the surface frame without saying so, directly above the box titled ORBIT SPEED. In translunar coast it reads '→ 11 923.3 m/s' over 'ORBIT SPEED 1 462.4 m/s'. That figure is the ground speed of a point co-rotating with Earth at 180 Mm: eight times the vessel's speed and above escape speed at that distance, so it reads as a broken number. In low orbit the same two places read 7 336.5 and 7 788.5 m/s, two answers to what looks like one question. A KSP player will ask which one is wrong.
findings.realReference: KSP shows one speed, in the frame its speed display names (surface, orbit or target), and in orbit mode it shows no surface horizontal speed. Flight displays (for example the Shuttle's entry displays, with separate inertial and Earth-relative velocity) label every velocity with its frame.
findings.likelyCause: src/ui/model.ts lines 100-102 (describeFlight): the altimeter always formats readouts.verticalSpeed and readouts.horizontalSpeed (surface frame), whatever the speed panel's surface/orbit mode.
findings.fixDirection: Make the altimeter's speed row follow the speed mode. In orbit mode, show the radial and horizontal components of the orbital velocity, so the row adds up to the ORBIT SPEED figure. Otherwise tag the row 'SRF', or hide the horizontal speed above the atmosphere. Add a unit test that in orbit mode the row's two components give back the orbit speed.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\flight-ui\real-lunarSurface-720p.png and real-lunarSurface-4k.png (the SURFACE SPEED box over the lander's legs and footpads); real-ascent-4k.png, lowOrbit-4k.png, pad-4k.png, chutes-4k.png (bottom cluster)
findings.defect: The bottom centre is a column of five separate pieces: the speed box, the pitch/heading/roll strip, the ball, the SAS plate and the gauge plate. It runs from y 471 to y 712 at 720p, the bottom 34 % of the frame in the middle of the screen, which is where the chase camera puts the vessel's lower end. In real-lunarSurface the SURFACE SPEED box covers the descent stage's legs and footpads and the ground they stand on, which is what a pilot watches when landing. The pieces also do not read as one instrument. There are three plates in two materials with gaps between them, and the speed box and the PRY strip float above the bezel, so the cluster looks like a set of web widgets rather than one shaped console (residual of the round-4 look item).
findings.realReference: KSP's and KSP 2's navball cluster: the speed readout sits on the ball's case, and the whole cluster stays in the bottom fifth of the frame, so a landing vessel's legs remain visible. The Apollo FDAI in C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\cockpit-interiors\apollo11-columbia-panel.jpg puts the ball, its rate needles and its readouts in one case.
findings.likelyCause: src/ui/hud/hudStyles.ts: the speed plate and the pitch/heading/roll strip are stacked above the bezel as separate plates. The SAS and gauge plates are separate islands. The hand-off declined a housing bar because of the 20 % coverage budget (the ascent is at 19.8 %).
findings.fixDirection: Put the speed readout on the bezel's top arc and set pitch and roll into the ring at 9 and 3 o'clock, with the heading on the lubber caret. That removes about 70 px of height at 720p and frees the coverage a shared housing needs. Join the SAS plate, ball and gauges on one gunmetal bar. Alternatively, or as well, have the chase rig (src/camera) frame a landed or near-ground vessel so its lowest point stays above the cluster. Re-shoot real-lunarSurface and check that the footpads show.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\flight-ui\pad-720p.png against ascent-720p.png (and pad-4k.png against ascent-4k.png); lowOrbit-720p.png against reentry-720p.png
findings.defect: The throttle and g tubes still move, now at liftoff and at entry interface. At 720p the gauge panel's top edge is at y 598 on the pad and y 575 in the ascent. The THROTTLE and G LOAD tubes, their scales and their values sit 23 px higher (about 69 px at 4K) once the G DOSE line appears. So the instrument shifts the moment the first stage lights, while the pilot is watching the throttle tube, and again when the vessel enters the air from orbit (598 in lowOrbit, 575 in reentry). The spec checks only reentry against entry-highg.
findings.realReference: The tape gauges in C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\cockpit-interiors\apollo11-columbia-panel.jpg never move, and shipped HUD gauge strips keep their scales in place through every flight phase.
findings.likelyCause: src/ui/hud/hud.ts and hudStyles.ts (.gauges .doseline): the dose row is reserved only where a dose can build ('in air, or above 0.5 g'), so it is absent when landed or prelaunch and in vacuum, and the bottom-anchored panel grows when the row appears.
findings.fixDirection: Reserve the dose row in every state (a dim 'G DOSE 0 %' or a blank row of the same height), or anchor the tube rows and give the dose line space below them that is always there. Extend the spec's g-tube bounding-box check to pad, ascent, lowOrbit and reentry.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\flight-ui\lowOrbit-720p.png (SAS plate x 416-528, y 640-695) and every other 720p view with the SAS plate
findings.defect: At 720p the eight SAS mode buttons, a primary control, are now the least legible marks on the HUD. The key digits are about 5-6 px tall and stand inside the icon box (the '5' runs into the anti-normal triangle). The icons are about 10 px across, so prograde, retrograde, radial-out and maneuver, which differ by small strokes, are hard to tell apart. The HUD's own floor is 10 px type (about 7 px caps), and the navball numerals were enlarged this round to meet it.
findings.realReference: KSP's SAS mode buttons at 720p carry icons of about 16-18 px, with the key in the tooltip. Shipped HUDs hold one minimum size for everything a player has to read.
findings.likelyCause: src/ui/hud/hudStyles.ts SAS mode grid: a 4 x 2 grid of buttons in a plate about 112 px wide at 720p. The key digit is a corner label inside each button and is not covered by expectTextFloor.
findings.fixDirection: Enlarge the mode buttons at 720p (icons about 15-16 px; the plate can grow by the width the gauges plate leaves free). Move the key digit out of the icon area, or into the tooltip and the key help. Add these labels to the text-floor check.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\flight-ui\attitude-lowOrbit-4k.png (lower rim: a translucent '40' under the maneuver marker near x 1830-1860, y 2020-2045, and a translucent '60' near x 2060-2090, y 1985-2010); lunarOrbit-4k.png (right-hand '20' and '-20' at reduced ink)
findings.defect: The half-cut and smeared numerals are gone; every numeral is now whole. A still frame still catches labels mid-fade, though, as pale watermark numerals at roughly a quarter to a third of full ink next to full-strength ones. In attitude-lowOrbit-4k two ghosts show at once in the lower half of the ball. At level attitude the right-hand column reads dimmer than the left. The hand-off states this as 'faint for a moment'.
findings.realReference: The FDAI in C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\cockpit-interiors\apollo11-columbia-panel.jpg: markings keep full contrast and pass under the case mask. KSP's rim numerals are foreshortened but solid.
findings.likelyCause: src/ui/navball/navballShader.ts labelVisibility: each label fades over about 0.04 R as its farthest corner nears the lip. Commit 2629739 narrowed the band, but it is still wide enough that most attitudes leave one label inside it.
findings.fixDirection: Narrow the per-label fade to about 0.01 R so a still almost never shows a ghost. Or let labels pass whole under the opaque lip, with a soft inner shadow on the lip so a glyph under it reads as occluded rather than cut, as on the FDAI. Re-shoot attitude-lowOrbit-4k and crop the lower rim.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\flight-ui\chutes-4k.png ('GROUND TRACK none'); mfd-pages-4k.png and mfd-pages-native.png ('PREDICTED ARRIVAL none'); mfd-pages-hover-4k.png ('TRACK · ARRIVAL none'); mfd-pages-native-reentry.png ('GEAR none', STG page); every stage stack ('Mains · cut chute · deploy chute'); failed-4k.png ('Restart scene'); keyhelp-4k.png; stage-lockout.png
findings.defect: The wording still shows its data-model origins in places. Raw lower-case 'none' values sit in tables whose other states are UP, OFF, FINAL and READY. The Mains stage's subtitle 'cut chute · deploy chute' reads as cancelling itself. The failure modal offers 'Restart scene', which is lab vocabulary. The key help spells key names ('Period', 'Comma', 'Slash', 'Minus', 'Backquote') instead of showing the key glyphs. The LAUNCH panel in stage-lockout shows a 'Moon' chip beside 'No target: pick a body'. On the entry STG page the two remaining stages stretch to twice the row height under an empty upper half.
findings.realReference: Shipped game interfaces (KSP 2, Microsoft Flight Simulator) use an em dash or a plain phrase for an absent value, name chute stages by the chute ('release drogues · deploy mains'), and draw key caps with their glyphs ('.', ',', '/', '-', '`').
findings.likelyCause: Literal 'none' strings in src/ui/model.ts and src/ui/mfd/mfdPainter.ts (for example line 263 for gear). Stage subtitles come from the generic event kinds and do not name the part. The failure-action labels come from the lab. The key help prints event.code names. The MFD staging list stretches its rows to fill the page height.
findings.fixDirection: Use '—', or say what is meant ('vertical descent', 'no gear'). Name the chute in each event ('release drogues', 'deploy mains'). Label the lab action 'Restart flight'. Map the code names to glyph caps. Make the Moon chip read as a button ('Target: Moon?'). Cap the staging-row height and anchor the rows to the bottom with a summary strip under them.
